region: Vellore region, Tamil Nadu, India (district and surrounding dry-tropical landscape)
scope_note: A curated, sourced starter checklist for plants likely to be encountered across the wider Vellore region. It is not an exhaustive flora or a claim that every listed plant occurs at every site. Presence is a library observation state, not a model prediction. A GBIF Plantae occurrence search for the Vellore-area bounding box returned 1,895 records and 300 species facets when checked on 2026-09-05; GBIF coverage and publisher licenses vary, so that result is context for breadth rather than a complete flora census.

species.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent and widely cultivated in tropical settlements.
species.conservation_status: Not threatened in the cited Kew profile
species.ecology: Large tropical strangling fig; aerial roots can develop into additional trunks.
species.short_notes: A very large tree with aerial prop roots and leathery, prominently veined leaves.

knowledge.text: Banyan is a large strangling fig native to the Indian subcontinent; aerial roots hang from branches and can develop into additional trunks.

species.native_status: Native range includes India from southeast Pakistan to Myanmar.
species.ecology: Tropical fig associated with warm forests, open ground and cultivated sacred sites.
species.short_notes: Recognizable by its heart-shaped leaves with a long tapering tip; commonly planted around temples.

knowledge.text: The native range of sacred fig extends from southeast Pakistan to Myanmar and includes India, Nepal and Bangladesh.

species.native_status: Native range is southwestern India; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
species.ecology: Tropical food tree with inflorescences and large fruits produced on main branches and trunk.
species.short_notes: Look for large rough fruits attached directly to the trunk or major limbs and broad glossy leaves.

knowledge.text: Jackfruit has a native range in southwestern India and is now widely cultivated in tropical regions.

species.native_status: Native range includes India and tropical and subtropical Asia; commonly grown in South Asian homes.
species.conservation_status: Least concern in the cited Kew profile
species.ecology: Aromatic herb of warm open habitats and household gardens.
species.short_notes: A strongly aromatic, branching herb; leaves may be green or purple and stems are often hairy.

knowledge.text: Holy basil is an aromatic herb widely cultivated around South Asian homes and temples; the cited Kew profile places its native range in India and tropical Asia.

species.native_status: Native to northern India and Pakistan; now widely cultivated throughout the tropics.
species.conservation_status: Least Concern (IUCN assessment cited by Kew)
species.ecology: Fast-growing drought-tolerant tree cultivated in gardens and farms; compound leaves and long pods are distinctive.
species.short_notes: Compound leaves, pale fragrant flowers and long slender pods give this tree its familiar local name.

knowledge.text: Moringa is native to northern India and Pakistan and is now widely cultivated throughout the tropics.

species.native_status: Native range extends from Bhutan to India; cultivated widely for fragrant flowers.
species.ecology: Fragrant evergreen shrub grown in warm gardens and used as an ornamental and cultural flower.
species.short_notes: Small glossy leaves and intensely fragrant white flowers, often double in cultivated forms.

knowledge.text: Arabian jasmine has a native range from Bhutan to India and is introduced or cultivated in many tropical regions.

species.native_status: Native to Kerala and Tamil Nadu in India.
species.ecology: A region-specific Western Ghats tree; a low-confidence image match must not be treated as a confirmed record.
species.short_notes: Included to keep a conservation-sensitive Tamil Nadu species visible in the regional checklist.

knowledge.text: Syzygium microphyllum has a native range in India, specifically Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

species.native_status: Kew records a native range from Assam to Indo-China and records India as introduced; widely planted across India.
species.conservation_status: Not threatened (Kew prediction cited on POWO)
species.ecology: A drought-tolerant tropical tree common in streets, farms and dry woodland plantings.
species.short_notes: Feathery pinnate leaves, small white flowers and yellow drupes; avoid treating a common name as a taxonomic confirmation.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online records Azadirachta indica as a tree of the wet tropical biome, native from Assam to Indo-China, with India listed among introduced areas.

species.native_status: Kew records a native range from Assam to southern China and widespread cultivation, including India.
species.conservation_status: Data deficient in the IUCN record shown by Kew
species.ecology: Evergreen tropical fruit tree with leathery lance-shaped leaves, terminal panicles and large drupes.
species.short_notes: Leaves are often coppery when young; fruit size, shape and colour vary greatly among cultivars.

knowledge.text: Mangifera indica is a tree native from Assam to southern China and is widely cultivated in tropical regions, including India.

species.native_status: Origin is uncertain; Kew describes it as widely cultivated throughout the tropics and possibly native to tropical Africa, Madagascar and/or India.
species.conservation_status: Not currently of conservation concern in the cited Kew profile
species.ecology: Large seasonally dry tropical tree with many small leaflets and brown, acidic, sausage-shaped pods.
species.short_notes: The combination of fine paired leaflets and brown curved pods is useful, but fruiting is seasonal.

knowledge.text: Kew describes tamarind as a tree up to about 30 m with paired leaflets and brown pods containing acidic pulp; its origin is uncertain because it has been cultivated since ancient times.

species.native_status: Native to western and southern India and Sri Lanka.
species.ecology: Seasonally dry tropical tree known for long hanging racemes of yellow flowers and cylindrical dark pods.
species.short_notes: Golden flower racemes are conspicuous in season; compound leaves and long woody pods persist after flowering.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online records Cassia fistula as native to western and southern India and Sri Lanka.

species.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent.
species.ecology: Thorny or unarmed tree with trifoliate leaves and hard-shelled fruits; found in warm tropical and subtropical habitats.
species.short_notes: Three-foliolate leaves, aromatic foliage and hard round fruits help distinguish it from other garden trees.

knowledge.text: Kew describes Aegle marmelos as a tree of the Indian subcontinent with digitately trifoliolate leaves and hard-shelled fruits containing orange-red pulp.

species.native_status: Native from tropical and subtropical Asia to the western Pacific, including India.
species.ecology: Shrub or tree often associated with seasonally dry habitats; distinctive thick-walled flattened pods.
species.short_notes: Glossy compound leaves and flattened, thick-walled pods; also known in India as karanja.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online records Pongamia pinnata as native from tropical and subtropical Asia to the western Pacific, including India.

species.native_status: Native from southern China to tropical Asia, including India.
species.ecology: Seasonally dry tropical shrub or small tree with thick leaves, milky latex and waxy star-like flowers.
species.short_notes: Milky sap can irritate skin and eyes; observe without handling and never infer edibility from an identification.

knowledge.text: Kew records Calotropis gigantea as native from southern China to tropical Asia, including India, and describes it as a shrub or tree of the seasonally dry tropical biome.

species.native_status: Native to tropical America; introduced into India according to Kew distribution data.
species.ecology: Thorny aromatic shrub that can form dense stands in disturbed ground and dry woodland margins.
species.short_notes: Small clustered flowers change colour as they age; leaves are rough and aromatic. Treat this as an invasive-watch entry, not a recommendation for planting.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online records Lantana camara as native to tropical America and introduced into India.

species.native_status: Native range is Central Malesia to the southwest Pacific; cultivated widely in India.
species.ecology: Tall unbranched palm with a smooth trunk, crown of pinnate leaves and familiar fibrous fruit.
species.short_notes: A palm, not a tree with branches: the leaf crown and smooth leaning trunk are diagnostic at a distance.

knowledge.text: Kew describes Cocos nucifera as a palm distinguished by a smooth slender trunk, crown of pinnate leaves and its well-known fruit; its native range is Central Malesia to the southwest Pacific.

species.native_status: Native to tropical and subtropical Asia, including India; cultivated bananas derive from this wild ancestor.
species.ecology: Giant herb arising from a rhizome; overlapping leaf bases form a pseudostem and large leaves.
species.short_notes: The apparent trunk is a pseudostem made of leaf bases; wind-split leaves are common and not necessarily disease.

knowledge.text: Kew describes Musa acuminata as the wild ancestor of cultivated banana, a giant herb with a pseudostem formed from overlapping leaf bases; its native range includes India.

species.native_status: A cultigen with a native range listed by Kew as Peru; introduced and cultivated in India.
species.ecology: Small fruit tree with pale peeling bark, opposite aromatic leaves and edible berries.
species.short_notes: Pale coppery bark and strongly veined leaves are useful field clues; fruit colour varies by cultivar.

knowledge.text: Kew describes guava as a small tree up to about 12 m with pale brown or copper-coloured flaking bark and elliptic leaves; its distribution includes introduced India.

species.native_status: Native to northeast tropical Africa; introduced into India according to Kew distribution data.
species.ecology: Fast-growing shrub or small tree of disturbed ground with large palmately lobed leaves and spiny seed capsules.
species.short_notes: Seeds are highly toxic if chewed; use the visual record only and do not handle fruit or recommend medicinal use.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online records Ricinus communis as native to northeast tropical Africa and introduced into India; it is a shrub or tree of the seasonally dry tropical biome.

species.native_status: Native to the Americas; introduced into India. Prosopis juliflora is a widely used alternative name.
species.ecology: Armed shrub or tree that can naturalize in dry disturbed ground and compete with native vegetation.
species.short_notes: Long spines and small paired leaflets are useful clues; the accepted Kew name is Neltuma juliflora, formerly Prosopis juliflora.

knowledge.text: Kew accepts Neltuma juliflora and lists Prosopis juliflora as a synonym; its native range is in the Americas and India is listed among introduced areas.

species.native_status: Native to Central America through Venezuela and Ecuador; introduced into India.
species.conservation_status: Least concern in the IUCN record shown by Kew
species.ecology: Large spreading tropical street and shade tree with bipinnate leaves that can fold in low light.
species.short_notes: Very broad crown and tiny paired leaflets; commonly planted as a large avenue or campus shade tree.

knowledge.text: Kew describes Samanea saman as a tropical tree often used as a street tree; its native range is Central America to Venezuela and Ecuador and India is an introduced area.

species.native_status: Native to Mexico through Venezuela; introduced and cultivated in India.
species.conservation_status: Least concern in the IUCN record shown by Kew
species.ecology: Small seasonally dry tropical tree with thick branches, milky latex and fragrant flowers.
species.short_notes: Flowers are fragrant and variable in colour; milky sap can irritate and should not be handled.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online records Plumeria rubra as native from Mexico to Venezuela and introduced into India.

species.native_status: A cultivated hybrid; Kew lists it as a cultigen and records it in India.
species.ecology: Shrub grown in warm gardens; large showy flowers occur in many cultivated colour forms.
species.short_notes: A garden hybrid rather than a single wild provenance; use flower colour only as supporting evidence, not as a species key.

knowledge.text: Kew treats Hibiscus × rosa-sinensis as a cultivated hybrid (a cultigen) and records it as introduced or cultivated in India.
